speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether a feasibility study is conducted regarding the options to renew vis-a-vis to rebuild the Bukit Panjang LRT system; (b) whether causes of past breakdowns will be better resolved and future occurrences prevented as Bombardier has also been involved in the reliability work carried out since 2016; and (c) whether the renewal process could have commenced before the first half of this year since Bombardier is responsible for the renewal project.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is because any suspension of the BPLRT during peak hours would require us to deploy 40 double-deck or 80 single-deck buses, at frequencies of as low as three minutes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The existing roads just cannot support such a level of bus deployment.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As Bukit Panjang is already built-up, there is also limited scope to expand the current road network and to build additional bus facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: These non-LRT options would have created severe traffic delays and unacceptable tradeoffs to commuters’ travelling experience.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Even if LTA were to implement strict bus priority measures at the expense of motorists, a trip between, say, Choa Chu Kang Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and Bukit Panjang LRT stations, which are less than three kilometres apart, would take at least half an hour by bus due to the heavy road congestion created.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Hence, LTA discussed the LRT renewal option with several established LRT manufacturers, including the existing supplier, Bombardier of Canada.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Bombardier’s proposal was selected because it could be completed sooner, without requiring major civil engineering works or extensive service closures.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Bombardier, having worked with LTA and SMRT since 2016 to improve the BPLRT's reliability, was also deeply familiar with the difficulties the system faced.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: LTA, SMRT and Bombardier have jointly analysed the root causes of past BPLRT breakdowns and delays.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: They were largely due to faults with the signalling, traction power and train propulsion systems.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: First, the train's signal collector shoes tend to lose contact with the signalling system’s signalling rail at sharp turns.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Second, the traction power system supplies electricity to the trains through the power rail.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Similar to the signalling system, a recurrent cause of faults is when the trains' current collector shoes dislodge from the power rail at sharp turns.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The renewal will enhance the power rail with more robust rail brackets and we will also relocate the joints to less severe curves.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Third, faults with the train propulsion system will be addressed when the first-generation fleet of 19 trains are replaced with new models which will come with a more reliable Alternating Current (AC) propulsion system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The new fleet will also feature enhanced redundancy and better air-conditioning performance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Beyond these engineering fixes, LTA will also install more condition monitoring features to support predictive maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: At the same time, SMRT has contracted Bombardier to provide long-term service support for the renewed BPLRT system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This contract engages Bombardier to provide more expedient technical, logistical and spares support, including training for SMRT’s maintenance staff to build up local expertise.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Design work for the renewal has already started.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But meanwhile, SMRT has also engaged Bombardier to provide technical support for the existing BPLRT system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: LTA, SMRT and Bombardier are committed to improving the reliability of the existing BPLRT by intensifying preventive and corrective maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The recently announced Sunday closures of the BPLRT have been very useful for SMRT’s engineering teams.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: We thank commuters for their understanding and patience.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: In short, things will get a lot better when we have completely renewed the BPLRT, which will be 2022-2024.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: But meanwhile, we are intensifying maintenance for the existing BPLRT, and that is why we needed additional engineering hours, and we have already stepped up doing so with the Sunday closures.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I am confident that we can do a better job than what is happening today.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The other LRT, which is Sengkang-Punggol, is doing more than 100,000 km.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: My instruction to SMRT and LTA is to, first, close the gap and then work towards exceeding Sengkang's achievement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So, today, it is 50,000; I am confident that within a couple of years, we can double it, but that is still not my final destination.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I think we can do much better than that.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for his comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In the United States (US), for example, Sir, for many of the decommissioned rail tracks, they use buses to run – they call it bus rapid transit.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, for Singapore's BPLRT, has the Minister considered running buses on the track if this LRT will not be useful or reliable?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Sorry, I must declare my interest as I am in the management team of ComfortDelgro, which includes Singapore Bus Services (SBS) Transit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But you cannot simply take the existing viaducts and then run buses on it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But we will make sure that it is a much better LRT.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I totally agree with the Minister that if we do an all-bus model on the roads of Bukit Panjang, it is going to be quite difficult.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: But could the Minister elaborate more on why we cannot refurbish the viaduct and allow buses to run on it?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Is there a kind of study to prove that it is not effective, or not cost-effective?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As I said, you cannot just simply take the existing viaducts, buy the buses and just run them on it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: You actually got to do extensive civil engineering work on the viaducts, which means closing the LRT service, tear down the viaducts, major sections of it, and redo, which means no BPLRT service for months.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Here is Er Dr Lee Bee Wah speaking as an engineer!

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And I confirm what she has just said.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I hope so, because if our car-lite Singapore vision arrives – not immediately, but in 20 years' time – when the next version of the BPLRT will also run out of economic life in another 20 to 25 years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Hopefully, by that time, Singapore is largely car-lite, few cars, on the roads, then the roads can be handed over to buses and we can tear down the viaducts, redo them and run buses on top of them, or have cyclists cycling on the viaducts – which is a suggestion from Minister Vivian Balakrishnan.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He envisages the day when you can cycle on the LRT tracks.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Maybe theme parks might adopt it to do something else, I do not know.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But I think those are further down the road.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We leave it to the future Minister for Transport.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Among the planned renewal works, one of those that the residents really like very much and welcome is the replacement of the 19 new trains.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But the not so ideal part is that the timeline appears to be quite a distant future.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Can I ask the Minister if he can find ways to bring the delivery of the train cars forward because the old ones are really quite worn out?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I think the Minister must have tried that before.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The rides are quite bumpy and the air-conditioning is always not working well.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, if the Minister can see if he can do something about it to bring it forward – 谋事在人。See if you can do it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: How fast they can build, whether there is a way to shorten it, they will try.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the existing trains, we can do something, especially the air-conditioning system.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Surely, we can do something about it, and we shall fix it this year if we can.
